headline: Topological frameworks model higher-order brain network dynamics and interventions
label: Topological Brain Network Dynamics
summary: Recent preprints apply Hodge-structured and topological signal processing methods to brain and wearable data streams, extending beyond pairwise network models.
synthesis: The dominant thread is the use of higher-order, topology-aware representations to model network dynamics. Two brain-focused preprints apply this directly. One proposes a counterfactual causal framework that treats disruptions and interventions as energy perturbations on network flows, using Hodge-based structure. The other integrates diffusion MRI and resting-state fMRI within a topological signal processing framework to infer higher-order brain interactions. A third preprint extends the same logic to multimodal wearable and environmental streams through a graph vector field for health risk assessment, drawing on simplicial complex learning. The published Koopman study is methodologically distinct, applying kernel-DMD to multiome time-series data. What is new is treating interaction structure beyond pairwise edges as an explicit object for causal and dynamical inference, rather than as a descriptive summary.
